selectionSystem.value: South Australia selects on merit. Onshore factors, in no particular order: English, years of experience, qualification level, salary and an assessment of the employer; EOI points are not a determining factor above 65. Offshore factors: English, years and field of employment, qualifications and EOI points. Priority-industry candidates whose occupation is 190-eligible may get a 190; others may get a 491.
selectionSystem.note: Priority industries differ between official pages: the 22 Oct 2026 update names building and construction, defence, education, engineering, health and manufacturing; the stream pages name construction, engineering, manufacturing, trades, health and education. 'High-ranking' candidates in other industries may also be considered. Fees: ROIs are free; $394 per nomination application.

cohorts.note: EOI with South Australia as first preference, under 45 when nomination is approved, competent English and 65+ points including nomination points.

status.note: Onshore ROIs are restricted from 22 October 2026.

restrictions.value: Onshore ROIs are open only to those living and working in South Australia whose current visa expires by 31 January 2027.

requirements.note: Current visa expires on or before 31 January 2027.

Read directly: lived in South Australia for the last 6 months, after completing the course. Our months question does not say whether those months came after completing the course, so this check is not applied as verified.

Read directly: worked full-time for 6 months after completing the course. Work must be in the same ANZSCO sub-major group (first 2 digits) as the nominated occupation. Our months question does not say whether those months came after completing the course, so this check is not applied as verified.

selectionSystem.value: WA ranks EOIs with no state score: by sector tier (building and construction trades; then building and construction non-trades, healthcare and social assistance, hospitality and tourism, education and training; then all other sectors), by WA residence, then by EOI points and EOI date. selectionSystem.note: Official pages conflict: the web FAQ ranks sector before residence, while the October 2026 last-invited PDF lists residence first, then sector. cohorts.note: No minimum residence, and offshore candidates are accepted. Those living in WA are ranked first and must show 3 months' continuous WA residence immediately before the invitation; those living interstate or overseas must show a genuine commitment to WA.
